THE OPEN LIST GROWS FASTER THAN THE WORK, IN THREE WAYS A FIRST-TIME USER FOUND IN ONE DAY. qs 2026-09-04, all three from the same document.

① ONE MISSING EDGE, THREE FINDINGS. 'A new capability that is satisfied, verified and realised but not yet ALLOCATED produces an "unallocated" gap, an "unrealized" gap (when the artifacts point at the component instead), and an "unthreaded cluster" defect. ALL THREE ARE CORRECT, but they are ONE MISSING EDGE SEEN FROM THREE ANGLES, and the repair guidance for the cluster ("no mechanical repair, a judgement only a person holds") is HEAVY FOR WHAT WAS A FORGOTTEN `allocate` CALL.'

② A GAP THAT CANNOT YET BE ANSWERED. 'The "20 verified capabilities not validated" gap is a good concept (built right vs the right thing) but IT FIRES AS ONE BLOCK THE MOMENT A DESIGN HAS VERIFICATIONS, BEFORE ANY VALIDATION IS POSSIBLE. A grace condition (only after a release or an epoch) would make it land when it can be acted on.'

③ THINKING OUT LOUD COSTS A GAP EACH TIME. 'Exploratory decisions connect to nothing by construction, so each one raises an "open idea connects to nothing" gap until the user picks. Reasonable, but IT MEANS THE GAP LIST GROWS WITH EVERY BRAINSTORM; a `kind: exploratory` node could be exempt until it becomes a choice.'

⭐ ③ IS THE SHARPEST BECAUSE IT PENALISES THE BEHAVIOUR THE PROJECT ASKS FOR. The brainstorm skill's whole argument is that an idea should enter the graph immediately and unpromoted; the skill's own text says it must not teach the user 'that thinking out loud has a cost'. It does have one, and it is one gap per idea. `kind: exploratory` is already recorded and already read by the linking discipline — the exemption has a field to key on and does not need new vocabulary.

⭐ AND ① IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE dev_storyflow COUNT FROM 2026-08-23 — 28 open `unsatisfied_requirement` gaps of which 8 were already `deferred`, a 29% noise rate on one class. Two projects, independently, reporting that the open list is inflated by findings nobody should be asked about. `acknowledge_gap`'s own description is the argument both of them quote back: A LIST THAT CAN NEVER REACH ZERO GETS SKIMMED.

⚠️ AND ALL THREE ARE CORRECT FINDINGS, which is what makes this hard rather than obvious. Nothing here is a false positive. The complaint is about AGGREGATION and TIMING — how many rows one cause produces, and whether a question arrives when it can be answered. A fix that suppressed any of them as noise would be deleting true information; a fix that GROUPS them by cause, or DELAYS them to when they are actionable, would not.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether reflow2's own graph shows the same three shapes. qs is a ~350-node design and this graph is 3,671; the ratios need not carry, and neither count has been taken here.
